_README: Host-anchored requisition ids: company-hosted boards whose ids the generic rules cannot
see. role-matcher.mjs (Node) and scripts/eval-blockers.py (Python) both read this file,
because neither can import the other, and a rule held in one of them only is a posting the
other cannot recognise: until 2026-10-13 eval-blockers had none of these, so a packet on
these hosts could only ever be matched to its report by an exact url.
CONTRACT, the same in both readers. `re` is a regular expression in the syntax JavaScript
and Python share, matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY (Python adds re.ASCII so \w and \d mean what
they mean in JavaScript) against the url TRIMMED with its query and fragment cut. Group 1
is the id, and the key is `<ns>:<id lowercased>`. Rules are tried in order and the first
match wins, BEFORE any generic rule: a rule that owns its host knows that host's id better
than a generic `/jobs/N` or `/<7+ digits>` rule, which otherwise claimed some spellings
first and keyed one Google posting two ways.
Every rule is anchored at its own HOST, because two rows with EQUAL ids merge, so a loose
rule that hands two postings one id does the damage the id exists to prevent. That is
also why a four-digit floor is allowed here, where the host fixes the position, and never
in a generic rule, where four digits is a year.
github.careers and atlassian.com are front ends over iCIMS, and their page id IS the iCIMS
requisition id, so all three spellings share one `icims:` key and the key drops the
portal, since one employer serves several. iCIMS numbers each customer from its own
counter, so that id is unique only WITHIN ONE EMPLOYER, which `per_employer` records.
Breezy carries it too: its key drops the board subdomain and nothing establishes that
its hex ids are unique across boards. A rule may omit it only when its host is one
employer's own (Apple, Google, EA), and every rule of one namespace must agree.
role-matcher's consumers compare ids within one company already (merge-tracker and
dedup-tracker filter by company first, eval-write keys on id plus company); a consumer
that compares across companies, as eval-blockers' report index does, must scope a
per_employer key by company or one employer's report answers for another's packet.
`example` and `key` are a case every reader asserts: test-all checks role-matcher and
eval-blockers --selftest checks itself, so a rule added here is tested in both with
nothing else to edit. Ids in examples are placeholders.

rules._why: Databricks' own career pages end the path with the Greenhouse job id, the same id its ?gh_jid= links carry, so both spellings share the gh: key. Unread, the slug form had no identity and merge-tracker could fold two different reqs together on a title match.
